column1: # The verdict vocabulary a counterpart's NOTES.md section table may use, and the
# class each verdict counts as. checks/verify-notes-rows.sh owns this file: it
# reads every `| §…` row of every section table under mods/, takes the verdict
# each Here cell begins with, and refuses a cell whose verdict is not published
# here. Nothing derives this table from the tables it governs.
# It exists because the denominator was a reader's interpretation of free prose.
# The sealed packages carried 240 rows whose Here cell used one of the four
# verdicts records/counterpart-checklist.md named, and 307 carrying something
# else, so for most of the wave the classification was one hand reading a
# sentence. The rows now begin with a published word, and the word is what the
# count is taken from.
# The three classes, and why each row lands where it does:
#   exercised         a rule of the specification runs in this package and a
#                     test of this package asserts the change it makes. The
#                     denominator's numerator.
#   declarable-only   the shape is present and no Ravel seam at the reviewed
#                     revision runs it. Inside the denominator, because the
#                     section is observable and unexercised: a later revision
#                     that grows the seam moves this row without moving the
#                     specification. "Not reached" belongs here rather than
#                     outside, because a thing that is present and unreachable
#                     is still a thing this package carries.
#   excluded          the specification excludes it, marks it not carried, or
#                     the package declined to ship it. Outside the denominator,
#                     because there is nothing here for a later revision to
#                     exercise.
# Matching is longest-verdict-first and word-bounded: a published verdict counts
# only where the Here cell begins with it and the next character is a space, a
# comma, a semicolon or the end of the cell. So "implemented as data" carries the
# verdict "implemented", and a cell that starts "declared and asked for through
# the SDK" carries no verdict at all and has to say which class it means.
